title: Who Pays for Glucose?
endLine: Blood glucose holds steady while the body rewrites who pays for it.

scenes.tts: The first film ended with the brain turning to ketone bodies. Now follow the blood from an overnight fast through five weeks without food. Glucose slips by only about one millimolar. Ketones climb from about a tenth of a millimolar to seven or eight. If glucose barely moves, who is paying for it?
scenes.narration: The first film ended with the brain turning to ketone bodies. Now follow the blood from an overnight fast through five weeks without food. Glucose slips by only about 1 mM. Ketones climb from about 0.1 mM to 7 or 8. If glucose barely moves, who is paying for it?
scenes.caption: The first film ended with the brain turning to ketone bodies. Now follow the blood from an overnight fast through five weeks without food. Glucose slips by only about 1 mM. Ketones climb from about 0.1 mM to 7 or 8. If glucose barely moves, who is paying for it?
scenes.visual: 16:9. Carry the first film's colour map unchanged: YELLOW glucose, ORANGE glycogen, PINK new glucose (gluconeogenesis), TEAL fatty acids, GREEN ketone bodies, RED muscle protein (the cost), PERIWINKLE brain, GOLD 'you are here', GREY organs and axes. New in this film: PALE TEAL for glycerol (fat's backbone) and WHITE dots for nitrogen. No molecular structures anywhere: labelled organ boxes, bars, gauges and flowing dots only. THE WORLD, kept all film: (1) TOP band: a time scrubber with five stops labelled '2 h', '12 h', '1 day', '3 days', '5 weeks' (from the lesson's fasting table), a small tag 'spacing schematic' under it, and a GOLD marker. (2) LEFT 25% of the frame, about 70% of its height: a tall blood tube holding two side-by-side vertical gauges on ONE shared scale 0 to 8 mM, ticks at 0, 2, 4, 6, 8: a YELLOW 'glucose' column and a GREEN 'ketones' column. Gauge heights are the midpoints of the lesson's table: glucose 6.5, 4.75, 4.25, 3.75, 3.75 mM; ketones 0.1, 0.15, 0.4, 2.5, 7.5 mM at the five stops. (3) RIGHT 30%: a PERIWINKLE brain box labelled 'brain', with a vertical bar beneath it labelled 'brain's glucose, g/day', scale 0 to 120 g, filled YELLOW to 120. (4) CENTRE, introduced in later scenes: GREY organ boxes 'liver', 'muscle', 'fat' (and later 'kidney'), never more than six things on screen in all. Link-back motion: on 'turning to ketone bodies', a few GREEN dots drift into the brain box and it glows once. On 'follow the blood', the GOLD marker sweeps the scrubber from '12 h' to '5 weeks' over about 6 s; the YELLOW gauge sinks only from 4.75 to 3.75 while the GREEN gauge rises from 0.15 to 7.5, overtaking it. A thin bracket on the YELLOW gauge labelled 'about 1 mM' marks the small drop. On the question, the marker snaps back to '12 h', the gauges reset, and large white text appears across the top: 'Who pays for steady glucose?' Ambient: blood dots drift slowly up the tube throughout.

Title 'Who Pays for Glucose?' fades in for 2 s above the world while the question text fades out. The gauges hold their 12 h values; blood dots keep drifting in the tube; the brain's YELLOW bar shimmers gently at 120.

scenes.tts: At first the liver pays from savings: its glycogen, about a hundred grams. Within a day or two, that store is mostly spent. After that, nearly all glucose must be made new.
scenes.narration: At first the liver pays from savings: its glycogen, about 100 grams. Within a day or two, that store is mostly spent. After that, nearly all glucose must be made new.
scenes.caption: At first the liver pays from savings: its glycogen, about 100 grams. Within a day or two, that store is mostly spent. After that, nearly all glucose must be made new.
scenes.visual: A GREY 'liver' box settles in the centre-left of the frame; inside it an ORANGE tank labelled 'glycogen ~100 g'. Show, then tell: the tank appears and settles before 'savings'. On 'pays', YELLOW dots stream from the liver into the blood tube, holding the YELLOW gauge steady. On 'within a day or two', the GOLD marker slides from '12 h' to '1 day' and on toward '3 days' while the ORANGE tank drains to a thin sliver (timing schematic); the GREEN gauge creeps up. On 'made new', a PINK label 'new glucose' lights inside the liver and the YELLOW stream out of the liver turns PINK-edged YELLOW. The YELLOW gauge never visibly falls more than the table values.

scenes.tts: Made from what? The fatty acids of fat cannot become glucose. Only fat's glycerol backbone can, about fifteen to twenty grams a day. The main raw material left is your own muscle protein.
scenes.narration: Made from what? The fatty acids of fat cannot become glucose. Only fat's glycerol backbone can, about 15 to 20 grams a day. The main raw material left is your own muscle protein.
scenes.caption: Made from what? The fatty acids of fat cannot become glucose. Only fat's glycerol backbone can, about 15 to 20 grams a day. The main raw material left is your own muscle protein.
scenes.visual: On screen: scrubber (marker at '3 days'), blood gauges, brain with its bar, liver, and two new GREY boxes that settle before they are named: 'fat' at lower right of centre and 'muscle' at lower left of centre, with a RED block inside muscle labelled 'protein'. On 'fatty acids', TEAL dots leave fat and enter the liver (they fuel it), but a RED barrier line drawn inside the liver marked 'no glucose' stops them from joining the glucose-making path. On 'glycerol backbone', a thin PALE TEAL stream labelled 'glycerol' enters the liver and passes the barrier into that path. On 'main raw material', a thick RED stream of dots leaves the muscle's protein block toward the liver, and the protein block shrinks slightly.

scenes.tts: Muscle protein is broken into amino acids. Alanine carries carbon and nitrogen to the liver. The carbon can become glucose; the nitrogen is dumped as urea. The kidney joins in more and more. By five weeks, it makes about as much glucose as the liver.
scenes.narration: Muscle protein is broken into amino acids. Alanine carries carbon and nitrogen to the liver. The carbon can become glucose; the nitrogen is dumped as urea. The kidney joins in more and more. By five weeks, it makes about as much glucose as the liver.
scenes.caption: Muscle protein is broken into amino acids. Alanine carries carbon and nitrogen to the liver. The carbon can become glucose; the nitrogen is dumped as urea. The kidney joins in more and more. By five weeks, it makes about as much glucose as the liver.
scenes.visual: Fat slides off the right edge for now (still six things at most). The RED stream from muscle becomes paired tokens labelled 'alanine', each a RED dot with a small WHITE dot attached (WHITE = nitrogen). Inside the liver each token splits: the RED part turns PINK and leaves as glucose into the blood tube; the WHITE part drops into a small outlet labelled 'urea' and flows away. On 'the kidney joins in', a GREY 'kidney' box settles below the liver and starts sending its own PINK-edged YELLOW stream into the blood. On 'by five weeks', the GOLD marker slides from '3 days' to '5 weeks' while the kidney's stream thickens until it matches the liver's; a small '=' sign appears between their two streams, labelled 'about equal'.

scenes.tts: Now total the brain's bill. Burning only glucose, it needs about a hundred and twenty grams a day. Glycerol covers fifteen to twenty. The rest would cost about a hundred and eighty grams of muscle protein daily. At that rate, a third of an adult's protein would be gone in about two and a half weeks.
scenes.narration: Now total the brain's bill. Burning only glucose, it needs about 120 grams a day. Glycerol covers 15 to 20. The rest would cost about 180 grams of muscle protein daily. At that rate, a third of an adult's protein would be gone in about two and a half weeks.
scenes.caption: Now total the brain's bill. Burning only glucose, it needs about 120 grams a day. Glycerol covers 15 to 20. The rest would cost about 180 grams of muscle protein daily. At that rate, a third of an adult's protein would be gone in about two and a half weeks.
scenes.visual: The kidney slides aside (off frame); the scrubber dims and its marker parks. The brain's bar grows to fill most of the right half: 0 to 120 g, labelled 'if only glucose'. On 'glycerol covers', the bottom of the bar fills PALE TEAL as a soft-edged band from 15 to 20 g, labelled 'glycerol 15-20 g'. On 'the rest', the remaining bar above it (about 100 to 105 g) fills RED, labelled 'from protein'. A RED arrow runs from that segment to the muscle box, where a label appears: '~180 g protein a day'. On 'a third of an adult's protein', the muscle's protein block is relabelled 'body protein ~10 kg' and a dashed line marks one third of it; a small day counter runs from 0 to about 18 days (computed: 3.3 kg at 180 g a day) as the block drains to that line, labelled '1/3 gone, ~2.5 weeks'. Tag at the bottom: 'rough sums'.

scenes.tts: Here is the whole idea. Blood glucose stays nearly level. Underneath, the body keeps changing who pays for it, and how much.
scenes.narration: Here is the whole idea. Blood glucose stays nearly level. Underneath, the body keeps changing who pays for it, and how much.
scenes.caption: Here is the whole idea. Blood glucose stays nearly level. Underneath, the body keeps changing who pays for it, and how much.
scenes.visual: The muscle block refills to full (reset, label back to 'protein'). Pull back to the full world: scrubber, blood gauges, brain with its RED and PALE TEAL bar, liver, muscle. On 'stays nearly level', the YELLOW gauge glows and a horizontal YELLOW line is drawn across it at about 4 mM, labelled 'nearly level'. On 'who pays', the payers pulse in turn under the gauge: ORANGE glycogen tank (thin), PALE TEAL glycerol stream, RED protein stream. On 'how much', the brain's bar pulses. Text at the bottom, white: 'level on top, changing payers below'.

scenes.tts: Ketones cut the brain's glucose need to about a third, roughly forty grams a day. Does muscle's share of the bill fall to a third as well? Or further?
scenes.narration: Ketones cut the brain's glucose need to about a third, roughly 40 grams a day. Does muscle's share of the bill fall to a third as well? Or further?
scenes.caption: Ketones cut the brain's glucose need to about a third, roughly 40 grams a day. Does muscle's share of the bill fall to a third as well? Or further?
scenes.visual: GREEN dots flow into the brain box. On 'about a third', the top of the brain's bar is replaced from the top down by a GREEN region labelled 'ketones instead', until the glucose part ends at 40 g on the 0 to 120 scale; a bracket labels the remaining glucose part '~40 g'. The PALE TEAL and RED segments inside that 40 g are NOT yet redrawn: the 40 g glucose part is a plain YELLOW outline. Question card at top in white: 'Muscle's share: a third, or less?' The muscle box's RED protein stream holds at its old width.
Predict pause. The question card stays. GREEN dots keep drifting into the brain; blood dots drift in the tube; the bar and the muscle stream hold still. No other change.

scenes.tts: Further: to about a fifth. In these rough sums, glycerol still covers its fifteen to twenty grams. So the whole cut comes off muscle's share.
scenes.narration: Further: to about a fifth. In these rough sums, glycerol still covers its 15 to 20 grams. So the whole cut comes off muscle's share.
scenes.caption: Further: to about a fifth. In these rough sums, glycerol still covers its 15 to 20 grams. So the whole cut comes off muscle's share.
scenes.visual: The question card dissolves. Inside the 40 g glucose part, the PALE TEAL glycerol band redraws at the same 15 to 20 g as before; the RED segment above it fills only the remaining 20 to 25 g. Beside the bar, a ghost of the old RED segment (about 100 to 105 g) stands next to the new one (about 20 to 25 g), with a label 'about 1/5' (computed: 22.5 / 102.5). On 'the whole cut', a GREEN bracket spans the 80 g removed and points to the RED ghost, showing the removed grams all came from the protein side. The RED stream from muscle thins to about a fifth of its old width.

scenes.tts: At that smaller bill, the fat, about seventy-five days of energy, runs out before the protein does. These sums show direction and size only. Measured protein loss in long starvation runs lower, nearer twenty grams a day.
scenes.narration: At that smaller bill, the fat, about 75 days of energy, runs out before the protein does. These sums show direction and size only. Measured protein loss in long starvation runs lower, nearer 20 grams a day.
scenes.caption: At that smaller bill, the fat, about 75 days of energy, runs out before the protein does. These sums show direction and size only. Measured protein loss in long starvation runs lower, nearer 20 grams a day.
scenes.visual: The fat box slides back in at lower right with a large TEAL block labelled '~75 days of energy'. Two horizontal drain bars appear side by side under muscle and fat, both labelled in days, schematic: the fat bar empties first while the muscle protein bar still holds more than half; a small tag 'fat runs out first'. On 'direction and size only', a tag 'rough sums' brightens. On 'measured', the RED stream from muscle thins a little further and a small label reads 'measured: ~20 g/day'.

scenes.tts: Back to five weeks. Blood glucose has barely moved. Behind it, the brain runs about two-thirds on ketones. The kidney makes about as much glucose as the liver. And muscle pays a fraction of its old bill.
scenes.narration: Back to five weeks. Blood glucose has barely moved. Behind it, the brain runs about two-thirds on ketones. The kidney makes about as much glucose as the liver. And muscle pays a fraction of its old bill.
scenes.caption: Back to five weeks. Blood glucose has barely moved. Behind it, the brain runs about two-thirds on ketones. The kidney makes about as much glucose as the liver. And muscle pays a fraction of its old bill.
scenes.visual: The drain bars and fat fade (six things: scrubber, gauges, brain with bar, liver, kidney, muscle). The scrubber brightens and the GOLD marker sits at '5 weeks'. Gauges at the table's 5-week values: YELLOW 3.75 mM, GREEN 7.5 mM. On 'barely moved', the YELLOW gauge glows. On 'two-thirds on ketones', the brain box fills as a pie: two-thirds GREEN, one-third YELLOW, labelled '~2/3 ketones'. On 'the kidney', the kidney returns below the liver with its stream matching the liver's, '=' sign shown. On 'muscle pays a fraction', the thin RED stream from muscle pulses beside a faint ghost of its old thick width.

scenes.tts: So the steady number in the blood hides a shifting bill. Glycogen pays first, then muscle protein. Then fat, through ketones, takes over most of the brain's fuel.
scenes.narration: So the steady number in the blood hides a shifting bill. Glycogen pays first, then muscle protein. Then fat, through ketones, takes over most of the brain's fuel.
scenes.caption: So the steady number in the blood hides a shifting bill. Glycogen pays first, then muscle protein. Then fat, through ketones, takes over most of the brain's fuel.
scenes.visual: The kidney slides aside and fat returns. The GOLD marker sweeps once from '12 h' to '5 weeks' over about 7 s, and the world replays in miniature: the YELLOW gauge holds nearly level throughout while the payer below it changes on cue. On 'glycogen pays first', the liver's ORANGE tank pulses and drains; on 'then muscle protein', the RED stream from muscle swells (near its peak about 3 days) and then thins; on 'then fat, through ketones', TEAL dots leave fat, turn GREEN in the liver, and flow into the brain, whose pie settles at two-thirds GREEN. The YELLOW 'nearly level' line stays drawn across the glucose gauge the whole time.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (blood dots drifting in the tube, GREEN dots flowing into the brain, a thin RED stream from muscle). Large centred white text: 'Blood glucose holds steady while the body rewrites who pays for it.'
